title: Domelipa, Now Known as Dome, Breaks Down 5 Essential Tracks From Debut Album ‘La Del Arroba’
summary: "I want to show the side of me that no one has seen through my music," says the influencer-turned-singer.
contentText:
Known on social media as Domelipa, the Mexican influencer-turned singer has decided to leave behind the part of her life that made her famous to pave the way for her music career under the name Dome. With this transition comes her debut album La Del Arroba , a 14-track set that ranges from Latin pop to electronic music and urban sounds.

“I want people to know more about me. I want to show the side of me that no one has seen through my music,” the 25-year-old singer says in an interview with Billboard Español . “The album talks about personal things with lyrics that go from nostalgic to joyful.”

Domelipa Talks Ozuna Collaboration & New Career Era With Sony Music Latin

Released on Thursday night (Sept. 24) under Lipa Music and distributed by Sony Music Latin, La Del Arroba features several collaborations. These include “@Ese Vato” with Ozuna, produced by Ovy On The Drums, which was released last July as the lead single. There’s also “@Bomba de Humo” with Corina Smith, “@Ojitos” with 3AM, “@Audemars” with Omar Montes and “@Una Señal” with Bolela.

Interestingly, all track titles begin with an “@” symbol, while the lyrics reference the codes of early social media, transporting listeners back to 2010.

Dome, born in Monterrey, Mexico, has over 75 million followers on TikTok. She is the second most popular user in Latin America on the platform and the seventh globally, making the name change on her social media a potentially significant challenge.

“When I made the change, it was a very strange feeling. At first, I was scared,” she confesses. “But in the end, it was liberating for me because I found the right way to tell my stories through the songs.”
